headline: VICTORIA GOLD SYSTEM GROWS: AMARA MINERALS HITS 102M AT 2.29 G/T AU WITH VISIBLE GOLD LOGGED IN FOURTH HOLE
snippet: Amara Minerals (ASX: AM3) has reported hole AA2603 at its Apollo project in central Victoria — 102.3m @ 2.29 g/t Au from 140.5m depth, including a 66.8m high-grade core at 3.08 g/t Au. A fourth hole has now logged visible gold with assays not expected until mid-November. Apollo sits in the Lachlan Fold Belt gold corridor that hosts several large deposits; the expanding intercept widths and consistent grade suggest a system with bulk-tonnage potential, and each drill release has pushed the defined footprint outward.

headline: STANDOUT CAPITAL EFFICIENCY: NORDIC RESOURCES LIFTS KOPSA GOLD 86% TO 1.52MOZ ON JUST 9,631M OF DRILLING
snippet: Nordic Resources (ASX: NNL) has delivered an interim resource update at its Kopsa project — 44.0Mt @ 1.07 g/t AuEq for 1.52Moz AuEq, an 86% increase on the prior resource achieved on only 9,631 total metres of drilling. The ounce-per-metre drilled ratio is among the more compelling in the current junior sector. The resource remains open in multiple directions and the company has indicated further drilling is planned for Q1 2027.

headline: GOLD ENTERS CRITICAL FOMC WEEK AT $4,210 — BULLS AND BEARS BOTH WATCHING OCT 27-28 FED MEETING FOR DIRECTIONAL VERDICT
snippet: Gold opened the week of October 12 near $4,210/oz, holding most of last Friday's 0.9% bounce after a weak US jobs report slashed Fed rate-hike odds from 70% to below 25%. Silver near $61/oz. Markets are in a holding pattern: the October 27-28 FOMC meeting is now the single most important binary catalyst for precious metals between now and year-end. A dovish hold validates the rebound; renewed hawkish guidance risks retesting the $4,100 support range. Junior miners watching closely — GDXJ has underperformed bullion by a factor of two since January's $5,589 gold peak.

headline: BHP ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS SAY DEAL 'FAR OFF' AS OCT 14 STRIKE DEADLINE AT WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE ENTERS FINAL HOURS
snippet: BHP Escondida supervisors (1,020 members, 95% strike vote on Oct 1) told reporters that collective contract talks remain 'far off' as government-mandated mediation enters its final window before an October 14 strike deadline. BHP formally requested mediation on October 5, triggering a 5-day window that expires this week. LME copper near $14,600/t — 2% below September's $14,875/t all-time record — as traders price potential disruption at the mine responsible for roughly 5% of global copper supply. Centinela, where a hunger strike has been ongoing since October 10, compounds the dual-threat picture for Chilean copper output.

headline: LARVOTTO HITS 20.5M AT 9.4 G/T AuEq AT HILLGROVE — NEW ECHIDNA LODE OPENS PARALLEL STRUCTURE BESIDE MIDAS
snippet: Larvotto Resources (ASX: LRV) has reported 20.5m @ 9.4 g/t AuEq at Blacklode within the Hillgrove gold-antimony system in NSW, and separately identified a new parallel structure — the Echidna Lode — beside the Midas zone. Seventeen more holes from the current campaign are still to be reported. Hillgrove's combination of high-grade, near-surface intercepts and structural complexity is building toward a maiden mineral resource estimate that the company has flagged for H1 2027.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING ACQUIRES MCEWEN'S TIMMINS GROUND FOR $55M — FULLER AND PAYMASTER PROPERTIES EXTEND DOME MINE FOOTPRINT
snippet: Discovery Mining has signed a US$55 million asset purchase agreement to acquire McEwen Mining's Fuller and Paymaster properties in the Timmins gold camp. Terms: US$5M cash plus US$50M in Discovery shares, with share count set by a 5-day VWAP pre-closing. The deal adds ground directly adjacent to the Dome Mine — one of Canada's longest continuously producing gold operations — and consolidates Discovery's strategic presence in the Abitibi gold belt. Closing expected late October 2026 subject to TSX approval.

headline: 20 OF 23 HOLES HIT SIGNIFICANT COPPER AT BOA RESOURCES RICCI LEE — BEST ASSAY 22M AT 3.05% CU INCL. 9M AT 6.86%
snippet: BOA Resources (ASX: BOA) has reported batch results from its Ricci Lee RC drilling program in Western Australia, with 20 of the first 23 holes returning significant copper mineralisation. The standout assay: 22m @ 3.05% Cu from 250m depth, including a 9m core at 6.86% Cu. Ricci Lee sits approximately 2km southwest of the Thaduna deposit analogue (4.1Mt @ 2.5% Cu). A further 40 RC holes and 92 air core holes remain pending across the broader Ricci Lee-Thaduna corridor.

headline: NEXGEN ENERGY'S ROOK I CONCRETE BATCH PLANT ARRIVES AHEAD OF SCHEDULE — KEY MILESTONE FOR CANADA'S BIGGEST URANIUM BUILD
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX/NYSE: NXE) reports an early delivery of the concrete batch plant at its C$2.2 billion Rook I uranium project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — a piece of critical infrastructure needed for underground shaft construction, targeted for early 2027. Construction started summer 2026 following federal licensing in March 2026; the airstrip and expanded accommodations are commissioned and occupied. Rook I is permitted for up to 30 million lbs/year uranium output and has a 24-year mine life in the feasibility study.

headline: KAZATOMPROM SHAREHOLDERS ABSTAIN ON ROSATOM URANIUM DEAL — STRATEGIC SIGNAL AS KAZAKHSTAN REDIRECTS SUPPLY TO WEST AND CHINA
snippet: At an October 7 extraordinary general meeting, holders of 88.34% of Kazatomprom voting shares abstained on approving a uranium supply contract with Russia's Uranium One group — while separately approving a parallel deal with China's SNURDC. Kazakhstan produces approximately 39% of global uranium supply. The effective rejection of the Rosatom-linked contract reinforces the strategic pivot of Kazakhstani uranium flows toward Western and Asian buyers, a structural positive for independent uranium producers and the current $97/lb long-term contract pricing environment.

headline: INDONESIA LAUNCHES $10.2 BILLION NICKEL DOWNSTREAM COMPLEX AND SHIPS FIRST-EVER EV BATTERY EXPORT
snippet: Indonesia opened 11 downstream battery-metals projects at the Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP) in North Maluku on October 8, with a combined investment of US$10.2 billion, and simultaneously shipped its first EV battery pack for export. The milestone marks Indonesia's transformation from raw nickel ore exporter to finished battery-cell producer — a supply chain shift with structural implications for nickel, cobalt, and manganese pricing as the country captures processing margin rather than only mining margin.

headline: GREEN & GOLD MINERALS HITS 27M ZONE AT MT GOSSAN; DRILLING COMMENCES AT MT WANDOO IN WA
snippet: Green & Gold Minerals (ASX: GG1) has reported a 27m mineralized zone at its Mt Gossan target in Western Australia while simultaneously commencing the maiden drill program at Mt Wandoo. The multi-target approach diversifies catalysts across the WA portfolio as the company works toward establishing a resource-definition target at one or more of its prospects. Assay results from both programs are expected over the coming weeks.

headline: WHY RECORD CENTRAL BANK GOLD BUYING ISN'T LIFTING MINING STOCKS — AND WHAT RETAIL INVESTORS IN JUNIORS NEED TO UNDERSTAND
snippet: An early-October analysis examines why gold mining equities have fallen 2-5x harder than bullion in 2026's correction — despite central banks buying a record 289 tonnes in Q3 and global gold ETF holdings hitting an all-time high of 4,256 tonnes. Attribution: company-specific execution failures (Sibanye, Harmony), cost inflation compressing margins at lower gold prices, and equity risk premiums expanding during rate-uncertainty environments. The piece argues the valuation gap between gold spot and miner equities is near historic extremes — a structural setup for mean reversion once the October 27-28 FOMC meeting resolves the near-term macro uncertainty.
